- Overestimate prices during sharp upward spikes in history; reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged downward trends; increase forecast mean slightly.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days; adjust forward by 1–2 days for near-term forecasts.
- Overshoots after high volatility periods; cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below true peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if history shows strong trend, forecast should revert to 30-day moving average within 5–7 days.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high volatility; dampen forecast sensitivity to last 5–7 days if volatility > 10%.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >15% in 3+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 5–10%.
- If model consistently underestimates true price in early days of forecast horizon, shift forecast upward by 2–5% for first 3 days.
